text:
alex: Quick sync - pros/cons: ephemeral per-tenant egress IPs vs regional shared egress gateway. Thoughts?

maria: Per-tenant ephemeral IPs -> mapping source IP -> tenant is trivial for audit/allowlists. Downside: IP exhaustion, allocation churn.

sam: Shared gateway reduces IP count and routing complexity, but you lose stable tenant IPs unless we add mapping (which increases surface). Bigger blast radius on gateway failure.

alex: Ops risk is real. HA active-active per-AZ possible but still larger fault domain. Also NAT throughput limits.

jordan: Security: customers love stable IPs for firewall rules. Shared gateway would need additional controls (per-tenant proxying or port-mapping) which many customers won't accept.

katie: Cost ops note - AWS account EIP limits + per-EIP spend adds up at scale. We should estimate SLO-driven allocation vs reuse.

sam: Proposal: hybrid mode. Allocate 1-2 stable IPs for high-SLA tenants, push low-volume tenants through shared gateway. Auto-promote on thresholds.

maria: Hybrid seems pragmatic. Also separate control-plane egress: use mTLS tunnels from tenant VPC agents to the private control plane regardless of egress design. Keeps control plane auth separate.

alex: For mTLS cert issuance flow: agent boot -> attestation -> short-lived cert. Eg:
```
# agent boot flow
curl -X POST https://cp.redwood.internal/attest -d '{"agent_id":"i-01234","sig":"..."}'
# response: {"cert":"PEM...","expires":"...""}
```

jordan: Need revocation plan. Short TTLs help but we should support immediate revocation via CRL or push policy to control plane. Also audit logs for cert issuance.

katie: If we do ephemeral IPs, we need an EIP pool manager service: allocate/attach/release, metrics, pre-warm NATs, respect AWS rate limits. I'll sketch a proto.

sam: For shared gateway, tenant identification options: source IP mapping (loses tenant separation), HTTP header injection (leaks tenant id to external services), or application-layer proxy (adds latency). None are perfect.

maria: Decision rubric idea: (1) Tenant requires stable allowlist -> stable IPs. (2) Tenant < X TPS & no allowlist -> shared gateway. (3) Provide automated migration + cost telemetry.

alex: Action items: 1) spike EIP pool manager prototype 2) run regional shared-gateway HA failure drill 3) design agent cert issuance + revocation. Volunteers?

sam: I'll run HA failure drill and document fallout.

katie: I'll build EIP pool manager prototype and add metrics.

jordan: I'll produce security checklist for cert TTLs, revocation, and tenancy leakage risks.

deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded: katie/eip-pool-proto -> staging (sha: abc123) :rocket:

alex: Nice. Let's reconvene next Wed with spike results. Thanks folks! :thumbsup:
